verdicts.statement: Theorem 1.7 (1.5). If $M$ is a manifold without boundary, then its $P$-category is at least one more than the $p$-length of $M$: $\mathop{\mathrm{P\text{-}cat}}M \geq \mathrm{long}^{p} M + 1$. If $M$ is a manifold with boundary, then its $P$-category is at least the $p$-length of $M$: $\mathop{\mathrm{P\text{-}cat}}M \geq \mathrm{long}^{p} M$.

Proposition 1.8 (1.6). Let $(N; \partial N)$ be obtained from the sphere $S^2$ by removing a finite number $s$ of open discs: $(N; \partial N) = (S^2 \setminus \bigcup_{i=1}^{s} D_i^2; \bigcup_{i=1}^{s} S_i^1)$, and let $(L; \partial L)$ be obtained from the projective plane $\mathbb{R}P^2$ by removing a finite number $k$ of open discs: $(L; \partial L) = (\mathbb{R}P^2 \setminus \bigcup_{i=1}^{k} D_i^2; \bigcup_{i=1}^{k} S_i^1)$. For $p = 0$ the $p$-length of a two-dimensional compact connected manifold equals: 1. one, if the manifold is homeomorphic to $(N; \partial N)$, to $(L; \partial L)$, or to the sphere $S^2$; 2. two, on the other manifolds. For $p = 1$ the $p$-length of a two-dimensional compact connected manifold equals: 1. zero, if the manifold is homeomorphic to the sphere $S^2$ or to the disc $D^2$; 2. one, on the other manifolds.

Theorem 1.9 (1.7). Let $M = S^{k_1} \times S^{k_2} \times \ldots \times S^{k_r}$ be a product of $k_i$-dimensional spheres, $i = 1, \ldots, r$, and let $p$ be a non-negative integer. Then $\mathrm{long}^{p} M \geq r - \min l(p)$, where the minimum is taken over all subsets $\{(k_{i_1}, k_{i_2}, \ldots, k_{i_l}) \subset (k_1, k_2, \ldots, k_r) : \sum_{j=1}^{l} k_{i_j} \geq p\}$.

Corollary 1.10 (1.8). Let $M = S^{k_1} \times S^{k_2} \times \ldots \times S^{k_r}$ be a product of $k_i$-dimensional spheres, $i = 1, \ldots, r$. Then the (co)homological length of $M$ equals the number $r$ of factors: $\mathrm{long}\, M = r$.
Proposition 1.11 (1.9). The $p$-length of the $n$-dimensional torus is $p$ less than its dimension: $\mathrm{long}^{p} T^n = n - p$.

Proposition 1.12 (1.10). The Lyusternik--Shnirelman category of a two-dimensional compact connected manifold with boundary, not homeomorphic to the disc $D^2$, equals two. Moreover, the categorical sets may be chosen so as to intersect only along their boundaries, and so that each is homeomorphic to the disc $D^2$.

Proposition 1.13 (1.11). The round category of a two-dimensional compact connected manifold equals: 1. one, if the manifold is homeomorphic to $S^1 \times I$ or to the Möbius band; 2. two, on the remaining manifolds with boundary; 3. two, if the manifold is homeomorphic to the sphere $S^2$, the projective plane $\mathbb{R}P^2$, the torus $T^2$ or the Klein bottle; 4. three, on the remaining manifolds without boundary.

Proposition 1.14 (1.12). The round category of a three-dimensional compact connected manifold without boundary 1. equals two if the manifold is homeomorphic to one of the following: the sphere $S^3$; $S^1 \times S^2$; the projective space $\mathbb{R}P^3$; a lens space obtainable as a quotient of $S^3$ by a differentiable action of the group $\mathbb{Z}_p$; 2. equals three on the torus $T^3$; 3. does not exceed four on the remaining manifolds.

Theorem 1.15 (1.13). Let $M = S^{k_1} \times S^{k_2} \times \ldots \times S^{k_r}$ be a product of $k_i$-dimensional spheres, $i = 1, \ldots, r$. Then the Lyusternik--Shnirelman category of $M$ is one more than the number $r$ of factors: $\mathop{\mathrm{cat}}M = r + 1$.

Theorem 1.16 (1.14). Let $M = S^{k_1} \times S^{k_2} \times \ldots \times S^{k_r}$ be a product of $k_i$-dimensional spheres, $k_i \geq 1$, $i = 1, \ldots, r$, and let $P = S^{k_{i_1}} \times S^{k_{i_2}} \times \ldots \times S^{k_{i_l}}$ be a submanifold of $M$, where $\{k_{i_1}, k_{i_2}, \ldots, k_{i_l}\} \subset \{k_1, k_2, \ldots, k_r\}$. Then the $P$-category of $M$ equals $\mathop{\mathrm{P\text{-}cat}}M = r - l + 1$.
Corollary 1.17 (1.15). Let $P$ be the $k$-dimensional torus. Then the $P$-category of the $n$-dimensional torus equals $T^k\text{-}\mathop{\mathrm{cat}}T^n = n - k + 1$, $n \geq k$.
Proposition 1.18 (1.16). Let $P$ be the $l$-dimensional sphere. Then the $P$-category of the $n$-dimensional sphere equals: 1. two, if $l < n$; 2. one, if $l = n$; 3. zero, if $l > n$.

Proposition 2.2 (2.2). Let $P$ be a smooth submanifold of dimension $p$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$, and let $f\colon P \times \mathbb{R}^{n-p} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a function with the properties: $f$ is continuous; the submanifold $P$ lies in a level surface; $f|_{P \times \mathbb{R}^{n-p}\setminus C}$ is differentiable and has no critical points. Then on $P \times \mathbb{R}^{n-p}$ there exists a function $F\colon P \times \mathbb{R}^{n-p} \to \mathbb{R}$, having the properties: $F$ has a unique critical submanifold $P$; $F|_{P \times \mathbb{R}^{n-p}\setminus C} = f|_{P \times \mathbb{R}^{n-p}\setminus C}$ for some compact set $C \subset P \times \mathbb{R}^{n-p}$.

Proposition 2.4 (2.4). Let $M^m$ be a smooth compact manifold with boundary $\partial M^m$, which is a disjoint union of closed subsets $M_1$ and $M_2$, and let $(M^m; M_1, M_2)$ admit a covering $\{Q_i\}_{i=1}^{3}$ by three closed submanifolds satisfying: $\mathop{\mathrm{Int}}(Q_i) \cap \mathop{\mathrm{Int}}(Q_j) = \emptyset$, $i \neq j$; $(Q_i, M_i)$ is almost diffeomorphic to $(M_i \times [0,1], M_i \times \{0\})$ for $i = 1, 2$; $Q_3$ is almost diffeomorphic to $P \times D^{m-p}$, where $P$ is a smooth submanifold of $M^m$ of dimension $p$; $Q_1 \cap Q_2$ is a smooth submanifold of $M^m \setminus \mathop{\mathrm{Int}}Q_3$. Then on $M^m$ there exists a $P$-function $F\colon M^m \to \mathbb{R}$ with the following properties: $F$ takes a constant minimal value on $M_1$; $F$ takes a constant maximal value on $M_2$; $F$ has no critical points on $M_1$ or $M_2$; $F$ has a unique critical submanifold $P$ lying in $\mathop{\mathrm{Int}}M^m$.

Theorem 2.6 (2.5). Let $M^m$ be a smooth compact manifold (with or without boundary), and let $M_1 \subset M_2 \subset \ldots \subset M_k = M^m$ be a filtration of $M^m$ by compact manifolds with boundary, satisfying: 1. $M_i$ are manifolds with boundary, $i = 1, \ldots, k-1$; 2. $M_i \subset \mathop{\mathrm{Int}}(M_{i+1})$, $i = 1, \ldots, k-1$; 3. $\partial M^m \subset M_k \setminus M_{k-1}$; 4. for each $i = 1, \ldots, k$, the manifold $(M_i \setminus \mathop{\mathrm{Int}}M_{i-1}; \partial M_{i-1}, \partial M_i)$ admits a covering by three closed subsets as in Proposition 2.4. Then on $M^m$ there exists a $P$-function with $k$ critical submanifolds.

Proposition 2.8 (2.7). An integral trajectory of $\mathrm{grad}\, f$ passing through an arbitrary point of $U$ either enters $P$, or leaves $P$, or reaches the boundary $\partial \overline{U}$ at some point.
Corollary 2.11 (2.10). The tubular neighbourhood of a critical submanifold $P$ in $M$ contains arbitrarily small cylindrical neighbourhoods of $P$.
Proposition 2.12 (2.11). The set $C_\varepsilon(P)$ is a neighbourhood of $P$ in $M$, that is, a subset of $M$ containing arbitrarily small tubular neighbourhoods of $P$ in $M$.

Theorem 2.13 (2.12). Let $M$ be a smooth compact connected manifold (with or without boundary), and let $f$ be a $P$-function on it which, in the case of a manifold with boundary, takes a constant maximal value on the boundary and has no critical points on the boundary. Then the number of critical submanifolds of $f$ is at least the $P$-category of $M$.

Theorem 2.16 (2.15). Let $\{k_{i_1}, \ldots, k_{i_l}\}$ be a subset of $\{k_1, \ldots, k_n\}$ positive integers. Let $P = S^{k_{i_1}} \times \ldots \times S^{k_{i_l}}$ be a product of $k_{i_j}$-dimensional spheres, $j = 1, \ldots, l$. Then on the manifold $M = S^{k_1} \times \ldots \times S^{k_n}$ there exists an exact $P$-function with $n - l + 1$ singularities.

Corollary 2.17 (2.16). Let $P$ be the $k$-dimensional torus, $k \leq n$. Then on the $n$-dimensional torus there exists an exact $P$-function with $n - k + 1$ singularities. In particular, an exact round function on the $n$-dimensional torus has $n$ singularities.
Theorem 2.18 (2.17). Let $P = S^n$ be the $n$-dimensional sphere. Then on the odd-dimensional sphere $S^{2n+1}$, $n \geq 1$, there exists an exact $P$-function with two singularities.
Proposition 3.1 (3.1). On a two-dimensional smooth compact connected manifold with boundary, not homeomorphic to the disc $D^2$, there exists an exact function with two critical points.

Theorem 3.2 (3.2). On a manifold homeomorphic to the sphere $S^2$, to the projective plane $\mathbb{R}P^2$, or to the disc $D^2$, there exist no round functions. On every other two-dimensional smooth compact connected manifold round functions exist.

Theorem 3.3 (3.3). On every two-dimensional smooth compact connected manifold not homeomorphic to the disc $D^2$, the sphere $S^2$ or the projective plane $\mathbb{R}P^2$, there exists an exact round function whose number of singularities equals: 1. two on the torus and the Klein bottle; 2. three on the remaining manifolds without boundary; 3. one on the annulus $S^1 \times I$ and on the Möbius band; 4. two on the remaining manifolds with boundary.

Theorem 3.4 (3.4). On every three-dimensional smooth compact connected manifold without boundary a round function exists. If the manifold is homeomorphic to one of the sphere $S^3$, the projective space $\mathbb{R}P^3$, the manifold $S^1 \times S^2$, a lens space, then it admits an exact round function with two critical circles. If the manifold is homeomorphic to the torus $T^3$, then it admits an exact round function with three critical circles. On every other three-dimensional smooth compact connected manifold there exists a round function whose number of singularities does not exceed four.
Theorem 3.5 (3.5). Let $P = S^{n-1}$ be the $(n-1)$-dimensional sphere. Then on the $n$-dimensional sphere there are no $P$-functions.

Theorem 3.6 (3.6). Let $P = S^1$ be the one-dimensional sphere, and let $n \geq 3$. Then on the $n$-dimensional sphere there exists a $P$-function whose number of singularities does not exceed $[n/2] + 1$.
